items.mnemonic: A HAND hefts a WEAPON, a blunt wooden club, and hurls it end over end at the straw target: THROW.
A stone ALTAR with offerings laid neatly on top; through it the gods SHOW their will to the village.
Under a LID, EIGHT seeds split open; then WALKING LEGS carry the seedling off somewhere new. Nothing stays as it was: CHANGE.
A HAND drives a NAIL home with one clean, ringing blow: HIT.
TEN workers fix one EYE on a bent rod and pull it over the angle of a FISHHOOK until the line runs perfectly STRAIGHT.
A cart frame with two matched stalls side by side, the primitive BOTH: it simply means BOTH.
A STAKE is driven in and a CRAFT-square laid beside it to mark out the ground; every rite begins with this measured setup: CEREMONY.
A SMALL BIRD huddles under a COVER wedged onto a heavy STONE and does not budge in the gale; of that you can be CERTAIN.
A tree with one big round FRUIT sitting in its crown, the primitive itself: FRUIT.
Under one ROOF sits an entire VALLEY, a house so roomy it can CONTAIN anything you bring.
A single STROKE slashes through the HEART and pins it to the board so it can never slip: WITHOUT FAIL.
WATER drips from the ROOF onto ONE STEM, which splits the drops into EIGHT dancing streams, a little show the rain puts on: PERFORM.
Two rivals grab the same BROOM, one BOUND UP at the top, the other yanking the HOOK at the bottom, and neither lets go: CONTEND.
People SAY their piece around a FIRE, and when it burns low they light a second FIRE and keep talking into the night: DISCUSS.
A PRIVATE cook, by MOON-light, flips a SPOON in each hand, a SPOON-juggling act nobody else in the kitchen can match: ABILITY.
A PERSON is told exactly where to STAND in the line-up; that spot is their RANK.
Under a NET, TEN helpers keep one EYE on the catch while a FISHHOOK pins it down right where they PUT it.
WATER lifts the LID off a PRIVATE pool and spills it down the slope into the RIVER: FLOW.
By a TREE, WALKING LEGS halt and a MOUTH announces who may pass the gate; it sorts everyone by STATUS.
A SPOON, an ARROW, a BEAK and a foot told to STOP: too many odd clues in one spot, and you begin to DOUBT the story.
A JAWBONE lies in the middle of the ROAD; travelers step around it and PASS on without a second look.
A CORPSE-stiff clerk slides a WRAP of forms through a MOUTH-sized window; this is the counter of the BUREAU.
Point the bird in the right DIRECTION, give the cage one sharp STRIKE, and off it flies: RELEASE.
A SMALL FRAME over a MOUTH, with a CLOTH apron hanging below: the shopkeeper's everyday outfit, the USUAL.
A DOG curled up on its BED; one look at how it lies tells you its CONDITION.
The KING sends his knights on a QUEST for one perfect jewel; it comes back polished and round as a BALL.
An EAR trained to catch the faint SOUND of a HALBERD being sharpened; that is the night guard's whole EMPLOYMENT.
The primitive BESTOW: a hand reaching down to pass something into another hand. GIVE.
A PERSON carries TWENTY dishes stacked on EIGHT trays up the shrine steps: OFFER.
Every STEP of the patrol with a WEAPON on the shoulder is part of the job, a ROLE to play.
TREE beams fitted into a LATTICE, crossbar over crossbar; that is how you BUILD a frame that stands.
Under the ROOF a SPROUT pushes out of a MOUTH-shaped pot, and a SWORD slices the clump cleanly in two: DIVIDE.
A DOLLAR SIGN hangs over a pile of SHELL money that keeps shrinking; every coin that leaves is an EXPENSE.
A PERSON presses a label one INCH onto the parcel and smooths it flat: ATTACH.
A STEM poking out of the top of a field plot; follow it down to find where it grows from, the REASON.
To SAY it clearly the speaker grows HORNS of emphasis, opens his MOUTH wide and plants his LEGS: EXPLAIN.
TWENTY times the MOUTH of the HUSBAND calls, but the SMALL BIRD will not come down from the branch: DIFFICULT.
A PERSON with a keen NOSE hides under a COVER, HEART pounding, then sets off on WALKING LEGS to help anyway: SUPERIOR in every way.
A grown man with a hairpin pushed through his topknot, the primitive itself: HUSBAND.
A RIGHT HAND winds a VINE round and round into a tidy coil, gathering every loose end: COLLECT.
A bundle of RICE straw and an AXE coming down through it in one blow: CUT OFF.
Two guards pace the STOCKADE along the ROAD in opposite directions; their steps never match, they DIFFER.
WATER splashes onto a SMALL candle flame under the MOON until it hisses out: EXTINGUISH.
LIGHTNING strikes the ALTAR and the whole crowd falls silent; a GOD has spoken.
One STROKE of the sower's arm scatters RICE across the RICE FIELD in strict order, row after row: NUMBER.
The HUSBAND draws a circle with his compass and makes everyone SEE the perfect line: RULE.
At the crossroads of GO stands a TREE with a single DROP of sap; the path you walk to master a skill is an ART.
A PERSON gathers GRASS and stores it under a CLIFF to UTILIZE through the long winter: PREPARE.
Under the ROOF one slanting STROKE and a SEVEN-shaped post hold up the walls, a plain little HOME.
Under the ROOF a SPROUT has pushed up through the floorboards and a MOUTH of rot gapes in the beam: HARM.
A SAKE JAR goes round the table and a SNAKE of guests takes one cup each: DISTRIBUTE.
In the GRASS lies a WRAP of cloth; a MOUTH shouts, a STRIKE hits the drum, and the watchman starts to SAY it to everyone: WARN.
Under a LID in a PRIVATE room a child is fed by MOON-light, month after month: RAISE.
Under a LEAN-TO, TWENTY squares of CLOTH are laid on the floor, one for each guest to sit on: SEAT.
You SAY the family's name, ask the DIRECTION, then walk over and knock on the door: VISIT.
A bare BONE left on the drill ground where one HALBERD crossed another HALBERD: all that is left to REMAIN.
An EYE rests on a TREE, and the HEART below starts turning the picture over into an IDEA.
NOW, this very moment, held tight inside the HEART: a lingering THOUGHT.
The SHELF is slipping off the wall; a neighbor's POWER shoulders it back into place: HELP.
SMALL sparks fly from under a COVER where someone's POWER is being spent all night long: LABOR.
A PERSON holds up a fish BONE beside a SWORD to show the class the shape of a clean cut: an EXAMPLE.
A MOON over a DOG dozing beside the FIRE; it is simply SO, the way things naturally are.
A STUBBORN man plants himself on the HILL and lets nobody past that line: LIMIT.
Down the ROAD rolls a HEAP of dropped apples, and a boy sprints after it: CHASE.
A merchant takes a STAND under a FRAME stall, LEGS planted, MOUTH calling out prices: COMMERCE.
GRASS on top, a TREE underneath, and a whole GENERATION of green growing between them: LEAF.
A PERSON shouts a message up to a CLOUD, and the cloud carries it on to the next town: TRANSMIT.
A PERSON lends a THOUSAND days of POWER to the VILLAGE harvest: WORK.
ONE board held firm in TWO HANDS; three STREAKS of the chisel, and a SHAPE appears.
The SUN sits like a LID over a MOUTH-shaped gate, with a SMALL town spread out below: postcard SCENERY.
GRASS, then WATER; WALKING LEGS slip on the wet blades and a MOUTH yelps all the way down: FALL.
A WOMAN holding her CHILD close, the oldest picture there is of what it means to LIKE someone.
A STUBBORN mule on the ROAD plants its hooves and backs up one pace at a time: RETREAT.
A gambler BOUND UP in debts hands over his very last SHELL: DEFEAT.
WATER ahead; from a LEAN-TO on the bank the ferryman's RIGHT HAND waves TWENTY passengers aboard to CROSS OVER.
A DROP slips from the HUSBAND's open hand, gone before he can close his fingers: LOSE.
A SHEEP's fleece measured against a CRAFT-square comes out a little long on one side: the DIFFERENCE.
A tree whose top bar reaches wider than the rest, the primitive TIP: the far END of the branch.
Under the ROOF a guard stays within an INCH of the door all night: PROTECT.
A girl with GRASS in her hair raises an ARM and opens her MOUTH to laugh: YOUNG.
GRAIN heavy on the stalk; a THOUSAND of them are saved by the VILLAGE for spring planting: SEED.
A SHEEP grown BIG and plump, its fleece glowing in the evening sun; to the farmer it is simply BEAUTIFUL.
A PERSON kneels under ONE roofline; a MOUTH speaks and a SEAL is pressed, an order that decides a LIFE.
A full WINE JUG set on the ALTAR in thanks, the surest sign of GOOD FORTUNE in the house.
The DECEASED emperor's son looks up at the MOON and dreams of being KING one day: HOPE.
Two wings beating against each other, never in step, the primitive WRONG: a thing that is simply WRONG.
A SMALL BIRD, crest feathers BOUND UP, turns its head to SEE the whole valley at once: VIEW.
Under the ROOF, by MOON-light, a RIGHT HAND feels along the ALTAR for whatever was moved; you GUESS what happened here.
